headline: Chips and Risk-On Breadth Carry Stocks Into the Weekend
body_html:
Friday's session closed on a broadly constructive note, with 412 of 549 names in our universe finishing higher as investors leaned into risk assets heading into the weekend. Semiconductors led all sectors, advancing 3.81%, buoyed in part by geopolitical developments suggesting a potential agreement between Iran and Oman over Strait of Hormuz passage — a signal that the most acute supply-chain anxieties tied to the region may be easing, at least for now. Homebuilders and software were close behind, gaining 2.61% and 2.31% respectively, while energy was the lone sector in the red, slipping 0.59% despite a modest oil-price lift on the Hormuz news.

The session's undisputed standout was Corsair Gaming, whose shares surged 35.25% — a single-day move that overshadowed everything else on the tape. Twilio added nearly 25% and Natera climbed 21.37%, keeping healthcare diagnostics in the conversation. On the other side, Trade Desk suffered a steep 21.9% decline, the sharpest drop among decliners, a reminder that even strong macro backdrops can mask idiosyncratic pain at the single-stock level.

The S&P 500's approach toward another record high, noted in several Friday narratives, lends the week's rally additional weight. With geopolitical headlines still fluid and the Senate advancing Russia sanctions that must clear the House, traders will spend the weekend parsing whether Friday's appetite for risk was a durable repositioning or simply end-of-week window dressing.

briefs.headline: Corsair Gaming Explodes Higher in Session's Biggest Single-Stock Move
briefs.body: Corsair Gaming shares rocketed 35.25% on Friday, making it the most dramatic mover across the entire universe. The gaming-hardware specialist attracted outsized volume, and the magnitude of the advance suggested news-driven conviction rather than a quiet drift. No other name on either side of the ledger came close to matching the move's sheer size.

briefs.headline: Iran-Oman Hormuz Talks Lift Sentiment, But Energy Equities Lag
briefs.body: A U.S. official signaled that a deal between Iran and Oman regarding Strait of Hormuz operations could be imminent, and crude prices ticked higher on the prospect of reduced disruption risk. Yet energy stocks finished as the session's only losing sector, off 0.59%, with oil-services name Innovex International dropping 8.7%, suggesting equity investors remain skeptical about the sector's near-term earnings trajectory.

briefs.headline: Celsius Holdings Jumps as Rockstar Founder Builds a Stake and Eyes the Top Job
briefs.body: Celsius Holdings surged 16.83% after reports that the founder of Rockstar Energy has accumulated a meaningful position in the beverage company and is pushing to assume the chief executive role. The activist angle injected fresh momentum into a name that had been searching for a catalyst, lifting it into Friday's top-five gainers.

briefs.headline: Trade Desk Posts Session's Steepest Decline Amid Sector Crosscurrents
briefs.body: Trade Desk fell 21.9%, the sharpest drop among decliners, as internet-advertising technology names struggled to keep pace with the broader market's enthusiasm. The selloff stood in stark contrast to software's 2.31% sector gain, illustrating how divergent outcomes can coexist within adjacent technology categories on the same trading day.

briefs.headline: Senate Clears Russia Sanctions Bill; House Vote Now in Focus
briefs.body: The U.S. Senate passed a Russia sanctions package championed by Senator Lindsey Graham, sending the legislation to the House for a final vote. The bill's progress adds another layer of geopolitical complexity for investors already navigating Middle East tensions, and traders will watch for any House scheduling developments over the weekend that could move defense- and energy-adjacent names early next week.

briefs.headline: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan Announce Mutual-Defence Pact Amid Regional Instability
briefs.body: Three major regional powers — Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan — pledged mutual defence commitments as turmoil across the Middle East continues to intensify. The agreement broadens the alliance architecture in the region and could have lasting implications for energy security, defense procurement, and emerging-market sovereign risk, themes already surfacing in weekend investor conversations following Friday's close.
